item.title: [문화] ‘Utterly compelling’: Black Gold, a raging oil field fire set to music, is like a scream from nature
item.description: Manchester Collective, Lakeside Arts, Nottingham This take on Luke Mombrea’s Novello-winning work about a fire that burned for two months in Santa Fe, had little need of its billowing video backdropPremieres are all well and good, but what about second performances, and third and fourth? We puzzle over the problem of new music, of how to build a living classical repertoire, while too often giving new works just one outing to make their case, audiences just one chance to hear them. How brilliant, then, to see American composer Luke Mombrea’s Black Gold – winner of a 2025 Ivor Novello award – at the centre of the Manchester Collective’s new tour: another chance to get our ears around this widescreen soundscape with its slippery electro-acoustic vistas.The fire that raged through the Santa Fe oil fields in 1928 burned for two months, swallowing up the surrounding desert in smoke and ash. Steel plate photographs show derricks dwarfed by pillars of flame and black billowing clouds. They’re the starting point for Mombrea’s chamber work, whose three movements for flute, cello, double bass and percussion were conceived in tandem with Nate Mohler’s monochrome, photo-manipulating video projections. item.title: [과학] Loneliness is making us sick, but we may be treating it all wrong
item.description: Loneliness can be surprisingly deadly, with previous research linking it to a roughly 30% increase in the risk of premature death. However, a new study warns that treating loneliness as a medical condition could distract from its deeper social causes. While healthcare professionals can offer support, lasting solutions may require rebuilding communities and fundamentally changing the way people live and work.
